question:
A 37-year-old man is brought to the emergency department following a motor vehicle collision. His temperature is 38.1°C (100.6°F), pulse is 39/min, respirations are 29/min, and blood pressure is 58/42 mm Hg. There is no improvement in his blood pressure despite adequate fluid resuscitation. A drug is administered that causes increased IP3 concentrations in arteriolar smooth muscle cells and increased cAMP concentrations in cardiac myocytes. This drug only has a negligible effect on cAMP concentration in bronchial smooth muscle cells. Which of the following sets of cardiovascular changes is most likely following administration of this drug?
 $$$ Cardiac output %%% Mean arterial pressure %%% Systemic vascular resistance $$$?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Drug administration -> Increased IP3 concentrations in arteriolar smooth muscle cells -> Vasoconstriction -> Increased systemic vascular resistance -> Increased mean arterial pressure -> Decreased cardiac output -> 80% CHAIN: Drug administration -> Increased cAMP concentrations in cardiac myocytes -> Positive inotropic effect -> Increased cardiac output -> Decreased systemic vascular resistance -> Decreased mean arterial pressure -> 75% CHAIN: Drug administration -> Negligible effect on cAMP concentration in bronchial smooth muscle cells -> No change in bronchial smooth muscle tone -> No effect on systemic vascular resistance -> No change in mean arterial pressure -> No change in cardiac output -> 80%
analysis: The drug described is likely a combination of a vasopressor affecting arteriolar smooth muscle cells and a positive inotropic agent affecting cardiac myocytes. The increase in IP3 concentrations in arteriolar smooth muscle cells would lead to vasoconstriction, increasing systemic vascular resistance. The increase in cAMP concentrations in cardiac myocytes would enhance cardiac contractility, potentially increasing cardiac output. The negligible effect on cAMP concentration in bronchial smooth muscle cells suggests minimal impact on bronchial smooth muscle tone.
